newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech registry starts stock trade disclosure Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: Czech registry starts stock trade disclosure Feb 3.

text.p: The Czech Central Securities (SCP) Registry said on Wednesday that from February 3 it would publish information about each trade it registers, on the next business day after the transaction is executed.
In a statement, director Jiri Sedlacek said the SCP would publish details including the security's identification (ISIN), the price, volume, place of transfer, and type of operation of each trade.
The data would be available from 8 a.m. (0700 gmt) daily.
The move has been called for by many market participants since the SCP is the point of execution of a majority of trades conducted since post-Communist share trading began in 1993.
It comes after years of harsh criticism from investors who took issue with transactions being simply registered at the SCP which did not disclose individual prices and volumes of trades.

Facing growing calls for more market transparency, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik agreed with market participants in December to compel the SCP to release individual trade data.
Sedlacek said the SCP was still negotiating with the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) and the automated small investor market RM-System, about cooperation in the release of the SCP data.
Earlier on Wednesday, the governing chamber of the Prague Stock Exchange agreed to begin to publish off-market trades conducted by its members beginning on March 3.
The PSE said it was still working out technical details for the publishing of its information, which will include the price and volume of each issue traded off-market by bourse members.
